details:
One thing that is really, really nice about Noenoe's shader is the fact that they added instancing to it. It's brilliant. (the standard shaders have it too.) Cubed's shaders look fantastic, but I'm not sure if they have that option. 

By enabling instancing, Unity uses GPU Instancing to draw (or render) multiple copies of the same Mesh at once, using a small number of draw calls. It is useful for drawing objects such as buildings, trees and grass, or other things that appear repeatedly in a Scene, like, for example, multiple copies of the same face mesh for layering out highlight materials. Many, many unoptimized PMX conversions have DOZENS of repeated materials on either the same mesh or copies of the same mesh. 

VRChat should consider making this a REQUIREMENT, or, if it can be enabled programmatically on existing assets regardless of the shader used - as it would make it so all identical avatars and object any one user is rendering are called exactly once. I wonder if the VRChat team could keep a copy of the popular shader packages in use, update them to be more optimized, and use THAT internal version in the game engine instead of calling the one the user included. 

GPU Instancing only renders identical Meshes with each draw call, but each instance can have different parameters (for example, color or scale) to add variation and reduce the appearance of repetition.

GPU Instancing can reduce the number of draw calls used per Scene, too. 

Instancing isn't ticked by default on default standard shaders. If you guys could enable that somehow it might improve performance quite a bit without changing the appearance of anyone's avatar.
title: Forced material instancing
